result.title: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate Q-matrices for diagnostic classification models that approximate expert specifications, but evaluations have focused on the final matrices, leaving the basis of individual item-attribute assignments unexamined. This opacity limits the responsible use of AI in measurement. We propose Reasoning-Trace Analysis (RTA), a framework in which an LLM generates attribute-labeled reasoning steps through chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting and these steps are analyzed to reconstruct, compare, and inspect each assignment. RTA is intended to supplement expert review and empirical validation. In a simulation study with perturbed fraction subtraction items, four LLMs recovered the required attributes and withheld attributes the items did not require. In an empirical study with 11 fraction subtraction items, responses from 536 examinees, four LLMs, up to three temperatures, and 100 replications per condition, CoT-derived Q-matrices overlapped substantially with the reference Q-matrix (mean overlap .809) but less than directly generated Q-matrices (.877), and they varied more across replications. Inspection of the traces linked disagreements to item-type coding, labeling rules, and how operations were expressed as steps. Q-matrices with similar overlap differed in fit to examinee responses. RTA provides inspectable evidence that matrix-level agreement and fit do not.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Reasoning-Trace Analysis 框架：用 CoT 提示让 LLM 生成带属性标签的推理步骤，再据此重建、比较和检查 Q 矩阵中每个题目—属性指派，并在扰动分数减法题模拟与 11 题、536 名被试的实证数据中比较其与直接生成 Q 矩阵的重叠度及拟合差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 用逐步推理轨迹回溯并审计每个结构化决策的做法，可能为 LVR 中「答案是否使用 latent 内容」的步骤级归因与人工可查性提供线索；但研究对象是文本 CoT 和测量学 Q 矩阵，不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，迁移需较多核查。
